title: Play, Explore, Explain: Cooperative Learning in Action
technology: Smartphone, tablet, or laptop; one shared device per small group is enough.

agenda.title: Play a short concept Bingo game
agenda.prompt: Think about a clue, mark a concept, and explain why it fits.

agenda.title: Notice what makes the learning cooperative
agenda.prompt: Choose a shared goal, give everyone thinking time, and agree how you’ll take turns.

agenda.title: Explore two activities with your group
agenda.prompt: Try one tool in each eight-minute round. Rotate roles and record what learners would explain.

agenda.title: Share what you discovered
agenda.prompt: Offer a short example, a piece of learning evidence, and one question.

agenda.title: Make one activity work for your classroom
agenda.prompt: Choose a learning goal, a prompt, a participation routine, and a check for understanding.

agenda.title: Explain what you’ll take with you
agenda.prompt: Answer a short retrieval check and name one adjustment you’ll try.

terms.clue: You close your notes and try to recall the idea before looking back.
A classmate explains why the answer makes sense, not just which option to click.
You point to a detail, example, or result that supports your claim.
A useful cue helps you correct a misconception and try again.
You describe how your thinking changed after the activity.
Your group works toward one product that needs everyone’s contribution.
You use what learners say or do to decide what teaching comes next.
You connect a new idea to an example and explain how they relate.

tools.name: Bingo Card Generator and Bingo Caller
tools.purpose: Review and explain a concept before marking it.
tools.task: Paste the eight workshop terms into a three-by-three card with a free center. Read a clue, let each person decide, then ask a teammate to explain why the term fits before marking.
tools.product: One marked concept with an explanation everyone can give.
tools.listenFor: An explanation that connects the clue to the concept, rather than a lucky match.

tools.name: Quiz and Flashcard Studio
tools.purpose: Recall first, compare reasoning, then use feedback.
tools.task: Import the workshop quiz CSV. Each person answers silently before the group compares reasoning. Reveal the explanation, then choose one item for another try. The current tool also uses the QuizSplat name.
tools.product: A revised answer and a reason for the revision.
tools.listenFor: Each person recalls before seeing a teammate’s answer.

tools.name: Meme Puzzle
tools.purpose: Use a puzzle reveal to invite explanations.
tools.task: Load the workshop question-and-answer CSV or choose a library activity. Before revealing a tile, ask one person to answer and another to explain or question the reasoning. Use the image as a conversation starter, not proof of understanding.
tools.product: One content explanation and one question worth discussing.
tools.listenFor: Reasoning about the content, beyond excitement about the hidden image.

tools.name: Story Wheel
tools.purpose: Explain the order and importance of events.
tools.task: Use the three-event seed-growing example. Choose the events, put them in order, and explain why the sequence makes sense. Try a different order and ask which explanation would need to change.
tools.product: A three-event wheel and a spoken explanation of its order.
tools.listenFor: A connection between events, not just a list.

tools.name: Dicebreaker Creator
tools.purpose: Give everyone a turn to elaborate and reflect.
tools.task: Paste one workshop prompt into each of the six face fields in the creator. Roll a prompt, allow quiet thinking, then invite a response and a follow-up from someone else. Let people pass, write, or speak through a partner.
tools.product: One explanation extended by a colleague’s follow-up.
tools.listenFor: An example or connection that adds meaning to the first answer.

tools.name: Fortune Wheel
tools.purpose: Use phrase recall as a starting point for meaning.
tools.task: Paste the workshop phrases into a custom puzzle set. After solving a phrase, explain it with a classroom example. Rotate the person proposing an answer so one confident voice does not take every turn.
tools.product: A solved phrase plus a classroom example.
tools.listenFor: A useful example; solving letters alone does not show understanding.

roles.name: Navigator
roles.task: Open the activity and invite others to direct the next action.

roles.name: Explainer
roles.task: Say why an answer or choice makes sense.

roles.name: Questioner
roles.task: Ask for evidence or an example; make space for another voice.

roles.name: Connector
roles.task: Record the group’s idea and connect it to a classroom goal.
